candidates.title: Current step in the step list is shown only by bold text, not exposed programmatically
candidates.description: Information conveyed by presentation should also be available in structure (1.3.1). The step list ('1. When', '2. Vehicle and waste', '3. Check and book') marks the current step only with bold weight. In the ARIA snapshots the list items carry no aria-current or other state, so a screen-reader user hears three identical list items and cannot tell which step they are on.
candidates.impact: Residents using VoiceOver or TalkBack on a phone may not know how far through the three-step booking they are.

locations.snippet: list "Steps": 1. When / 2. Vehicle and waste / 3. Check and book

evidence.detail: list "Steps" > listitem: 1. When (no current state); same on vehicle and confirm snapshots
'2. Vehicle and waste' drawn bold; the others regular

factor_notes.impact: orientation only; the h1 partly compensates

candidates.recommendation: Add aria-current="step" to the current list item (or visually hidden 'current step' text) in the shared step component.

candidates.title: 'Few left' slots are moved visually above the Morning heading, away from their programmatic group
candidates.description: Visual grouping and the programmatic structure should agree (1.3.1). The slot grid uses CSS order:-1 to pull every 'Few left' slot to the top, above the 'Morning' heading, at 320 px and 1280 px. In the DOM and ARIA snapshot these buttons stay under 'Morning' or 'Afternoon' in time order, so afternoon slots such as 13:40, 14:00 and 16:40 appear visually above 'Morning' and outside the 'Afternoon' group. Sighted readers see one order and grouping, screen-reader users hear another. The tool already reported the resulting focus-order jump (2.4.3), so this record covers only the grouping mismatch.
candidates.impact: A resident with low vision who also uses a screen reader or magnifier may hear '13:40' under 'Afternoon' but find it above 'Morning' on screen. They may also read the top row as the earliest slots and book the wrong time.

locations.snippet: <button type="button" class="slot" data-slot="08:20" aria-pressed="false" style="order:-1">08:20 Few left
button "13:40 Few left" (under heading "Afternoon" in ARIA)

evidence.detail: 10 'Few left' slots (08:20 to 16:40) drawn above the 'Morning' heading
heading 'Morning' [3] > 08:00, 08:20 Few left, …; heading 'Afternoon' [3] > … 13:40 Few left, 14:00 Few left …

factor_notes.frequency: every day with any 'Few left' slot, i.e. most days
factor_notes.impact: misreading of slot time and group; screen-reader/visual mismatch

candidates.recommendation: Keep slots in time order under their heading and mark scarcity with the existing 'Few left' tag. If a 'nearly full' shortlist is wanted, render it as its own labelled group in the DOM rather than by CSS order.

candidates.title: Selected day button differs from unselected days only by a 1 px thicker border and a 1.16:1 tint
candidates.description: A state indicator needed to identify the selected control should be perceivable, at 3:1 against the adjacent state (1.4.11). The auditor judges state indicators (contrast check note). In the day group the pressed 'Saturday 17' has the same border colour as the other days (rgb 39,104,74) but 2 px wide instead of 1 px. Its fill rgb(227,242,235) against the unselected white is about 1.16:1 (sampled from the 1280 px capture), and the text weight is the same. Under forced colours the only remaining cue is the 1 px border difference. By contrast, the selected slot and vehicle buttons add bold text.
candidates.impact: Older residents with low vision may not see which day is chosen, and may book a slot on the wrong day.

evidence.detail: forced colours: selected day distinguishable only by border width

factor_notes.impact: may confirm a wrong day; the slot header 'Saturday 17 October' gives a text cue further down

candidates.recommendation: Give the pressed day the same bold-text treatment as pressed slots or a filled dark background with light text, or add a check icon. Keep an outline-based cue that survives forced colours.

candidates.title: Cancelled booking page is headed 'Booked' and tells the resident to show the reference at the gate
candidates.description: Headings should describe the topic or purpose of the content (2.4.6). On the cancelled-status done page, the h1 is still 'Booked'. The 'Your reference' section says 'Status: cancelled. This booking is not on the gate's list.' and then, unchanged, 'Show this at the gate…' and 'A reminder will be sent…'. A screen-reader user moving by headings hears 'Booked' and may never reach the status line. The status itself is red bold text, which is also text, so 1.4.1 is not involved.
candidates.impact: A resident whose booking was cancelled may drive to the centre and be turned away at the gate, which the product brief names as the costly failure.

evidence.detail: heading 'Booked' [1]; paragraph 'Status: cancelled. This booking is not on the gate's list.'; paragraph 'Show this at the gate…'

factor_notes.persistence: until the page template varies by status

candidates.recommendation: Make the h1 and the instructions follow the status, e.g. 'Booking cancelled', and drop the gate and reminder text when the booking is not on the list.

candidates.title: 'Change slot' returns to the day picker with 'Today' selected, not the booked day
candidates.description: Information the user already entered in a process should be auto-populated or offered for selection (3.3.7). From the confirm page for Saturday 17 October 09:20, 'Change slot' links to index.html with no day. The day picker then shows 'Today' pressed and the slot list empty while it loads. Choosing 10:00 and Next produced a booking for Monday 12 October 10:00, not 17 October. Vehicle, waste and personal details were kept. The resident must notice the day change and choose the day again, and must type it again in full if it came from 'Another day'.
candidates.impact: Residents changing a booking 'to the afternoon' may move it to a different day without noticing, then arrive on the wrong day and be turned away. Residents with memory or attention difficulties carry the extra re-entry.

evidence.detail: fill details → click 'Change slot' → step-07: day 'Today' pressed, no slots; click 10:00 → Next → final: 'Day Monday 12 October, Slot 10:00 to 10:20'; details kept

factor_notes.frequency: every use of the core change-slot task

candidates.recommendation: Carry the booked date (and slot) in the Change slot link so the day picker opens on that day with it pressed.

candidates.title: Expired-slot message does not say what to do next and blanks the slot
candidates.description: An error message should say how to recover (H9; CPY-04). When the held slot has gone, the summary reads only 'This slot is no longer available.' It is plain text, not a link. The booking summary replaces the slot time with '—', so the resident no longer sees which slot they lost. The way forward, the small 'Change slot' link in the summary, is not named in the message. Entered details are kept, which helps.
candidates.impact: A resident whose hold lapsed may press 'Book this slot' again, or give up, instead of choosing another slot.

locations.snippet: alert "There is a problem" > listitem: This slot is no longer available.

evidence.detail: listitem text without link; definition 'Slot': '— · Change slot'

candidates.recommendation: Name the lost slot and link to the slot list for the same day, e.g. 'Saturday 17 October 09:20 has just been taken. Choose another slot' linking to the day.

needs_human.what: Screen-reader pass of book-a-slot (critical) and change-slot with VoiceOver on iOS Safari and TalkBack on Android Chrome, as PRODUCT.md asks. Check the slots status is announced after picking a day, the error summaries, the pressed day/slot, and the confirm-to-done transition.
Read the slot grid with a screen reader and compare with the visual order of 'Few left' slots (CSS order:-1) at 375 px and 1280 px; decide whether the sequence still makes sense.
Hold a slot on the confirm page and wait: record how long the hold lasts, whether any warning appears before it lapses, and whether it can be extended.
Read each route's document title (/, vehicle, confirm, done booked/cancelled) and confirm each is descriptive and distinct.
Confirm no instruction depends on shape, position or colour (spot check of all copy, including the permit info panel).
Confirm a booking can be reviewed before submission and cancelled afterwards by the phone route in the done page.
Real browser zoom to 400% and text-only zoom to 200% on the slot grid (the emulation already shows 15 px overflow at 320 px).
A real Windows contrast theme: check the selected day is still identifiable and the focus indicator on slot buttons is visible.
Speech control (Voice Control on iOS): activate 'Another day' (a button styled as a link) and the icon-only info button by voice.
Keyboard-only run of the full booking at 200% zoom; the slot grid has about 30 tab stops plus the known missing focus indicators.
